es: Distinguir imply, infer, suggest e indicate (quién da a entender, quién deduce y con qué fuerza los datos apuntan a una conclusión) y valorar qué implica un texto sin sacar conclusiones precipitadas.

vocabulary.es: implicación, lo que se da a entender

teaching.en: A careful writer may imply a criticism without ever naming it, leaving readers to work out what was really meant.
teaching.es: Un autor cuidadoso puede insinuar una crítica sin nombrarla nunca, y deja que los lectores averigüen lo que se quería decir realmente.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply lo hace quien habla o escribe: da a entender sin decirlo.
segments: A careful writer may imply a criticism without ever naming
it, leaving readers to work out what was really meant.
teaching.audioText: A careful writer may imply a criticism without ever naming it, leaving readers to work out what was really meant.

teaching.en: Although the director never complained, the long silence after my question made me infer that she was not entirely satisfied.
teaching.es: Aunque la directora nunca se quejó, el largo silencio tras mi pregunta me hizo deducir que no estaba del todo satisfecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Infer lo hace quien escucha o lee: saca la conclusión por sí mismo a partir de una pista.
segments: Although the director never complained, the long silence after my
question made me infer that she was not entirely satisfied.
teaching.audioText: Although the director never complained, the long silence after my question made me infer that she was not entirely satisfied.

teaching.en: The survey results suggest that most commuters would switch to trains if the tickets were cheaper, although the sample is small.
teaching.es: Los resultados de la encuesta sugieren que la mayoría de los viajeros cambiaría al tren si los pasajes fueran más baratos, aunque la muestra es pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest: los datos apuntan a algo posible, sin certeza.
segments: The survey results suggest that most commuters would switch to trains
if the tickets were cheaper, although the sample is small.
teaching.audioText: The survey results suggest that most commuters would switch to trains if the tickets were cheaper, although the sample is small.

teaching.en: The laboratory readings indicate that the river is contaminated, so the evidence is firm enough to justify an immediate warning.
teaching.es: Las lecturas del laboratorio indican que el río está contaminado, así que las pruebas son lo bastante firmes como para justificar una advertencia inmediata.
teaching.explanationEs: Indicate señala con más firmeza que suggest; evidence es incontable: no lleva -s.
segments: The laboratory readings indicate that the river is contaminated, so
the evidence is firm enough to justify an immediate warning.
teaching.audioText: The laboratory readings indicate that the river is contaminated, so the evidence is firm enough to justify an immediate warning.

teaching.en: A tentative conclusion admits its limits, whereas people who jump to conclusions treat a single clue as if it were proof.
teaching.es: Una conclusión provisional reconoce sus límites, mientras que quienes sacan conclusiones precipitadas tratan una sola pista como si fuera una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Tentative = cauteloso y provisional; jump to conclusions = decidir sin pruebas suficientes.
segments: A tentative conclusion admits its limits, whereas people who jump to
conclusions treat a single clue as if it were proof.
teaching.audioText: A tentative conclusion admits its limits, whereas people who jump to conclusions treat a single clue as if it were proof.

teaching.en: To read between the lines, ask what the writer wants you to conclude and what the implication of each phrase might be before you draw a conclusion.
teaching.es: Para leer entre líneas, pregúntate qué quiere el autor que concluyas y cuál puede ser la implicación de cada frase antes de sacar una conclusión.
teaching.explanationEs: Implication: lo que un texto da a entender sin decirlo; no es lo mismo que lo que afirma.
segments: To read between the lines, ask what the writer wants you to conclude and
what the implication of each phrase might be before you draw a conclusion.
teaching.audioText: To read between the lines, ask what the writer wants you to conclude and what the implication of each phrase might be before you draw a conclusion.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las estanterías vacías la llevaron a deducir que algo iba mal.»

feedback.es: Sara no recibe la información: la deduce ella a partir de pistas, y eso es infer.

hint.es: Quien lee las pistas y saca la conclusión es quien deduce.

origin.text: Nobody told Sara that the shop was closing. However, the empty shelves and the worried faces of the staff led her to ___ that something was wrong.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que reparte bien los papeles de quien escribe y quien lee.

choices.text: The writer infers blame; the readers imply who is responsible.
The writer implies blame; the readers infer who is responsible.
The writer suggests blame; the readers indicate who is responsible.

feedback.es: El informe da a entender la culpa sin nombrarla (imply) y quienes lo leen deducen quién es el responsable (infer).

hint.es: El que escribe deja caer la idea; el que lee la deduce.

origin.text: The report says that a number of departments exceeded their budgets. It never names the sales team, but its readers quickly work out who is responsible.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La encuesta sugiere que la mayoría del personal prefiere trabajar desde casa.»

answer.text: The survey suggests that most staff prefer working from home

feedback.es: Con datos como sujeto, suggest that + oración presenta una conclusión posible, sin certeza.

hint.es: Los datos (the survey) son el sujeto de suggests.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su tono parecía dar a entender dudas» y «dedujeron que venía una votación».

feedback.es: La alcaldesa es quien deja caer la idea (imply) y los periodistas son quienes sacan la conclusión (infer).

sentences: The mayor never said that the plan was bad, but her tone seemed to ___ that she had serious doubts about it.
After listening to the speech, the journalists were quick to ___ that a vote was coming.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué hizo la directora en la reunión.

choices.text: She accused the whole team of hiding its figures.
She asked two managers to explain their delay afterwards.
She hinted at certain departments without naming them.

feedback.es: La directora aludió a ciertos departamentos sin nombrarlos: los gestos de dos jefes bastaron para que todos dedujeran a quiénes se refería.

origin.audio: In Monday's meeting, the director said that some departments have not yet sent their figures. She named nobody, but two managers looked at the floor, and everyone understood exactly whom she meant.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que expresa.

pairs: The email implies that jobs may go.

pairs.es: El texto insinúa algo sin decirlo

pairs: Staff infer that jobs may go.

pairs.es: Los lectores deducen por su cuenta

pairs: The figures suggest that jobs may go.

pairs.es: Los datos apuntan a algo posible

pairs: The figures indicate that jobs will go.

pairs.es: Los datos señalan algo con firmeza

feedback.es: Imply e infer son las dos caras de emisor y receptor; suggest e indicate gradúan la fuerza de los datos.

pairs: The email implies that jobs may go.

pairs.es: El texto insinúa algo sin decirlo

pairs: Staff infer that jobs may go.

pairs.es: Los lectores deducen por su cuenta

pairs: The figures suggest that jobs may go.

pairs.es: Los datos apuntan a algo posible

pairs: The figures indicate that jobs will go.

pairs.es: Los datos señalan algo con firmeza

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué reprocha la consultora al boletín.

choices.text: It reports results for only some of the departments.
It exaggerates the results of the three best departments.
It conceals that two departments are losing money.

feedback.es: La consultora reprocha que el boletín solo cuente tres departamentos y calle los otros dos, sin afirmar que exagere ni que pruebe un fracaso.

origin.audio: On this week's podcast, an adviser reviews a company newsletter. She points out that the editor wrote that sales rose in three departments but never mentioned the other two. The figures do not prove that those teams struggled, she says, yet what was left out is revealing. A reader who jumps to conclusions may blame the managers, whereas a careful reader simply notes what the newsletter does not say and asks to see the numbers.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender la consultora sobre los números que faltan.

choices.text: That the editor hid bad news from the staff on purpose.
That the numbers left out should be requested before deciding.
That the three departments reported are probably exaggerating.

feedback.es: Su consejo es pedir las cifras ausentes antes de juzgar: la omisión es reveladora, pero no prueba mala intención.

origin.audio: On this week's podcast, an adviser reviews a company newsletter. She points out that the editor wrote that sales rose in three departments but never mentioned the other two. The figures do not prove that those teams struggled, she says, yet what was left out is revealing. A reader who jumps to conclusions may blame the managers, whereas a careful reader simply notes what the newsletter does not say and asks to see the numbers.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las cifras indican claramente que el agua no es potable.»

feedback.es: Con cinco lecturas idénticas, los datos señalan algo con firmeza: indicate, más fuerte que suggest.

origin.text: The test was repeated five times, and every reading was the same. The figures clearly ___ that the water is unsafe to drink, so the warning is justified.

prompt.es: Elige qué actitud muestra la autora de la carta hacia el artículo.

choices.text: She agrees with the article but wants more praise for the cafés.
She rejects the tram line because it has harmed local shops.
She doubts the article because it ignores the shops that closed.

feedback.es: La autora reconoce lo positivo, pero subraya lo que el artículo calla: su actitud es de escepticismo educado; no afirma que el tranvía haya hecho daño ni rechaza todo el artículo.

origin.text: Dear Editor, I read with interest your claim that the new tram line has improved the city centre. You mention the cleaner air and the new cafés, but you do not say a word about the shops that have closed since March.

prompt.es: Elige qué da a entender la jefa con su último comentario.

choices.text: That extra effort may count when promotions are discussed.
That promotions have already been promised to certain people.
That anyone who refused extra shifts will be fired.

feedback.es: La jefa no promete nada, pero sugiere que quien ayudó será recordado cuando se hable de ascensos: es una implicación, no una afirmación.

origin.text: Thank you all for your help this month. I know that several of you covered extra shifts, and I am sure the team will remember who stepped forward when promotions are discussed.

prompt.es: Completa: «El tenso silencio en la sala dejaba pocas dudas sobre lo que pensaban todos.»

feedback.es: El silencio tenso es la pista de la que parte quien deduce lo que nadie dice en voz alta.

origin.text: Nobody mentioned the missing report during the meeting. Even so, the tense ___ in the room left little doubt about what everyone was thinking.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lee entre líneas antes de sacar conclusiones precipitadas.»

answer.text: Read between the lines before you jump to conclusions

feedback.es: Leer entre líneas pide contrastar cada pista con el texto antes de decidir, no después.

title.es: Apuntar a y dar peso a una tesis

es: Formular inferencias con point to, lend weight to, cast doubt on y consistent with, distinguir pruebas circunstanciales de pruebas corroboradas y usar must have / can't have para deducir el pasado.

teaching.en: The muddy footprints under the window point to someone who came in from the garden, although they do not identify the thief.
teaching.es: Las huellas de barro bajo la ventana apuntan a alguien que entró desde el jardín, aunque no identifican al ladrón.
teaching.explanationEs: Point to: la evidencia (sujeto) apunta hacia una explicación sin afirmarla.
segments: The muddy footprints under the window point to someone who came
in from the garden, although they do not identify the thief.
teaching.audioText: The muddy footprints under the window point to someone who came in from the garden, although they do not identify the thief.

teaching.en: A second witness who saw the same van that night would corroborate the first account and lend weight to it.
teaching.es: Un segundo testigo que hubiera visto la misma furgoneta esa noche corroboraría el primer relato y le daría peso.
teaching.explanationEs: Lend weight to: refuerza una tesis; corroborate: confirmar con una fuente independiente.
segments: A second witness who saw the same van that night
would corroborate the first account and lend weight to it.
teaching.audioText: A second witness who saw the same van that night would corroborate the first account and lend weight to it.

teaching.en: A receipt stamped at half past eight would cast doubt on his claim that he was at home all evening.
teaching.es: Un recibo sellado a las ocho y media pondría en duda su afirmación de que estuvo en casa toda la tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Cast doubt on: debilita una tesis; doubt aquí es incontable, sin a ni plural.
segments: A receipt stamped at half past eight would cast doubt
on his claim that he was at home all evening.
teaching.audioText: A receipt stamped at half past eight would cast doubt on his claim that he was at home all evening.

teaching.en: His account is consistent with the camera footage, but that alone does not prove it, because it is only circumstantial evidence.
teaching.es: Su relato es coherente con las imágenes de la cámara, pero eso por sí solo no lo prueba, porque es solo una prueba circunstancial.
teaching.explanationEs: Consistent with: encaja con la prueba sin demostrarla; circumstantial = indirecta.
segments: His account is consistent with the camera footage, but that alone
does not prove it, because it is only circumstantial evidence.
teaching.audioText: His account is consistent with the camera footage, but that alone does not prove it, because it is only circumstantial evidence.

teaching.en: The front door was locked from inside and the garden path is full of muddy prints, so the thief must have come through the garden; he can't have used the front door.
teaching.es: La puerta principal estaba cerrada con llave por dentro y el camino del jardín está lleno de huellas de barro, así que el ladrón debe de haber entrado por el jardín; no puede haber usado la puerta principal.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: casi seguro; can't have + participio: casi imposible.
segments: The front door was locked from inside and the garden path is full of muddy prints,
so the thief must have come through the garden; he can't have used the front door.
teaching.audioText: The front door was locked from inside and the garden path is full of muddy prints, so the thief must have come through the garden; he can't have used the front door.

teaching.en: Because circumstantial evidence proves little on its own, a careful investigator asks whether a second source can corroborate it.
teaching.es: Como las pruebas circunstanciales demuestran poco por sí solas, un investigador cuidadoso se pregunta si una segunda fuente puede corroborarlas.
teaching.explanationEs: Una inferencia sólida suma fuentes independientes en lugar de repetir la misma pista.
segments: Because circumstantial evidence proves little on its own, a careful
investigator asks whether a second source can corroborate it.
teaching.audioText: Because circumstantial evidence proves little on its own, a careful investigator asks whether a second source can corroborate it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las botas embarradas apuntan a alguien que trabajó en el jardín.»

feedback.es: La evidencia (las botas) es el sujeto y apunta hacia una explicación: point to.

hint.es: Evidencia + verbo + to; el sujeto es plural.

origin.text: The muddy boots by the back door ___ to someone who has been working in the garden, but they do not tell us who it was.

prompt.es: Elige el efecto de la foto sobre la versión de Sara.

choices.text: The photo lends weight to her story.
The photo is consistent with her story.
The photo casts doubt on her story.

feedback.es: Si ella dice que estuvo en casa y la foto la sitúa en la estación a la hora del robo, su versión queda en entredicho: cast doubt on.

hint.es: La prueba contradice lo que ella cuenta.

origin.text: Sara says she spent the whole evening at home. However, a photo shows her at the station at seven o'clock, exactly when the money disappeared from the shop.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su versión es coherente con la hora que figura en el recibo.»

answer.text: His story is consistent with the time on the receipt

feedback.es: Be consistent with + nombre expresa que la versión encaja con la prueba, sin demostrarla.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto tiene la imagen de la cámara sobre el relato de la testigo.

choices.text: It backs up what she described without settling the case.
It identifies the thief and settles the case for good.
It goes against the time that she gave the police.

feedback.es: La cámara refuerza la descripción de la testigo (lend weight to), pero el hablante aclara que no prueba que el hombre sea el ladrón.

origin.audio: The shop camera shows a man in a red coat at ten o'clock. That lends weight to the witness's story, because she described the same coat, although it does not prove that the man is the thief.

prompt.es: Completa: «La llave pone en duda su versión» y «el barro da peso a su idea».

feedback.es: Cast doubt on debilita una tesis y lend weight to la refuerza; con sujeto singular ambos llevan -s.

sentences: The key found in his pocket ___ doubt on his story.
The mud on the floor ___ weight to her idea that someone came in from the garden.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el efecto que describe.

pairs: The muddy footprints point to the garden.
A second witness lends weight to her story.
The receipt casts doubt on his claim.
His story is consistent with the camera.

feedback.es: Cada expresión gradúa la fuerza de la prueba: apunta, refuerza, debilita o simplemente encaja.

pairs: The muddy footprints point to the garden.
A second witness lends weight to her story.
The receipt casts doubt on his claim.
His story is consistent with the camera.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige qué concluye la agente sobre las pruebas.

choices.text: They prove that the suspect entered through the window.
They all point the same way, but a witness is still needed.
They show that the suspect was far away at the time.

feedback.es: La agente considera que las pruebas son solo circunstanciales y que hace falta un testigo antes de acusar a nadie.

origin.audio: At the hearing, the police officer summarised the case. The muddy footprints pointed to the garden, and the broken window suggested that someone had broken in from outside. However, the receipt found in the suspect's coat cast doubt on his claim that he had spent the evening at his sister's house, since it showed that he had bought fuel near the school at eight o'clock. Even so, she insisted that the evidence was only circumstantial, and that a witness would have to corroborate it before anyone could be charged.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué actitud muestra la agente ante el recibo.

choices.text: She regards it as decisive evidence against the suspect.
She rejects it because the time on it may be wrong.
She takes it seriously but will not treat it as proof.

feedback.es: Reconoce que el recibo pone en duda su versión, pero insiste en que es circunstancial: lo valora sin tratarlo como prueba definitiva.

origin.audio: At the hearing, the police officer summarised the case. The muddy footprints pointed to the garden, and the broken window suggested that someone had broken in from outside. However, the receipt found in the suspect's coat cast doubt on his claim that he had spent the evening at his sister's house, since it showed that he had bought fuel near the school at eight o'clock. Even so, she insisted that the evidence was only circumstantial, and that a witness would have to corroborate it before anyone could be charged.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes de aceptarlo, necesitamos un segundo testigo que lo corrobore.»

feedback.es: Corroborate significa confirmar con otra fuente independiente; una sola declaración no basta.

origin.text: The account of the first witness does not settle anything. Before we accept that the thief came through the garden, we need a second witness to ___ it.

prompt.es: Elige cómo matizar la conclusión rotunda de su hermana con la evidencia.

choices.text: Leo's footprints and coat point to him, but we need more evidence.
Leo must have been the thief, so there is no need to look further.
Leo can't have been the thief, because his coat was in the garden.

feedback.es: Una conclusión prudente usa la evidencia como sujeto (point to) y admite que faltan pruebas; las otras afirman o descartan sin base.

origin.text: Leo's footprints are next to the broken window, and his coat was found in the garden. His sister says: Leo is the thief, and that is a fact.

prompt.es: Elige la deducción más lógica sobre cómo entró el ladrón.

choices.text: The thief can't have come in through the window at all.
The thief must have broken the window from outside.
The thief must have broken the window from inside.

feedback.es: Los cristales caen dentro de la casa: la ventana se rompió desde fuera, y por eso se deduce con must have.

origin.text: The glass from the broken window is lying on the floor inside the house, not outside in the garden, and the lock on the front door has not been touched.

prompt.es: Completa: «No puede haber estado en la estación cuando desapareció el dinero.»

feedback.es: Can't have + participio expresa una deducción de imposibilidad sobre el pasado.

origin.text: She was with me at the cinema all evening, so she ___ have been at the station when the money was stolen.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las huellas por sí solas no prueban nada, pero apuntan a alguien de fuera.»

answer.text: The footprints alone prove nothing but they point to someone from outside

feedback.es: Point to + persona: la evidencia sugiere una explicación aunque no la demuestre.

title.es: Lo que la carta no dice

es: Inferir con prudencia lo que una carta personal no dice (soledad, protección, eufemismos) y justificar cada inferencia citando la frase que la apoya.

vocabulary.es: eufemismo, dicho con menos fuerza de la real

teaching.en: The house is very quiet now, wrote Gran, and because she never says that she feels lonely, we can only infer that she misses Sara.
teaching.es: «La casa está muy tranquila ahora», escribió la abuela, y como nunca dice que se siente sola, solo podemos deducir que echa de menos a Sara.
teaching.explanationEs: Quiet y lonely: la emoción no está escrita, se infiere de la pista.
segments: The house is very quiet now, wrote Gran, and because she never says
that she feels lonely, we can only infer that she misses Sara.
teaching.audioText: The house is very quiet now, wrote Gran, and because she never says that she feels lonely, we can only infer that she misses Sara.

teaching.en: She watered the plants every day and mended the gate without being asked, which suggests that she is reliable rather than merely helpful.
teaching.es: Regó las plantas todos los días y arregló la verja sin que se lo pidieran, lo que sugiere que es de fiar y no solo servicial.
teaching.explanationEs: Una acción repetida apunta a un rasgo de carácter; rather than matiza la inferencia.
segments: She watered the plants every day and mended the gate without being
asked, which suggests that she is reliable rather than merely helpful.
teaching.audioText: She watered the plants every day and mended the gate without being asked, which suggests that she is reliable rather than merely helpful.

teaching.en: When Gran tells Leo that Sara is busy, she may be trying to protect her, although the letter never says so directly.
teaching.es: Cuando la abuela le dice a Leo que Sara está ocupada, puede que intente protegerla, aunque la carta nunca lo dice directamente.
teaching.explanationEs: May introduce una inferencia prudente: es una posibilidad, no un hecho.
segments: When Gran tells Leo that Sara is busy, she may be
trying to protect her, although the letter never says so directly.
teaching.audioText: When Gran tells Leo that Sara is busy, she may be trying to protect her, although the letter never says so directly.

teaching.en: People who write that you should not worry about them usually want to reassure the reader, yet they may downplay a real problem.
teaching.es: Quienes escriben que no te preocupes por ellos suelen querer tranquilizar al lector, pero pueden quitar importancia a un problema real.
teaching.explanationEs: Reassure y downplay: lo dicho puede contradecir lo sentido.
segments: People who write that you should not worry about them usually want
to reassure the reader, yet they may downplay a real problem.
teaching.audioText: People who write that you should not worry about them usually want to reassure the reader, yet they may downplay a real problem.

teaching.en: Calling a week alone at home a little quiet is an understatement, and a careful reader notices how much the phrase plays down.
teaching.es: Llamar «un poco tranquila» a una semana sola en casa es un eufemismo, y un lector atento nota cuánto resta esa frase.
teaching.explanationEs: Understatement: decir menos de lo real; suele ocultar lo que más importa.
segments: Calling a week alone at home a little quiet is an understatement,
and a careful reader notices how much the phrase plays down.
teaching.audioText: Calling a week alone at home a little quiet is an understatement, and a careful reader notices how much the phrase plays down.

teaching.en: A writer may drop a hint on a postcard, and a good reader will quote the exact words that support each inference.
teaching.es: Un autor puede dejar caer una pista en una postal, y un buen lector citará las palabras exactas que apoyan cada inferencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Quote la frase y explica qué deduces de ella: la cita es la prueba de tu inferencia.
segments: A writer may drop a hint on a postcard, and a
good reader will quote the exact words that support each inference.
teaching.audioText: A writer may drop a hint on a postcard, and a good reader will quote the exact words that support each inference.

prompt.es: Elige la inferencia mejor apoyada por la carta.

choices.text: Gran probably misses Sara but does not say so.
Gran is annoyed that Sara has not written more.
Gran is worried about the plants and the gate.

feedback.es: La frase sobre la casa tranquila es la pista: sin reproches ni quejas, lo más prudente es que echa de menos a Sara.

hint.es: Busca la frase sobre la casa y piensa qué sugiere.

origin.text: Dear Sara, thanks for the postcard. The house is very quiet now, but the plants are fine. I fixed the gate and your brother called twice. Take your time. Love, Gran

prompt.es: Completa: «La abuela escribió que la casa está muy tranquila ahora.»

feedback.es: Quiet es la palabra de la pista: describe la casa sin ruido y de ahí se infiere la soledad.

hint.es: ¿Qué adjetivo dice que no hay ruido?

origin.text: Gran wrote, The house is very ___ now. She never says that she feels lonely, but the word makes us infer it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Deduzco que la abuela quiere protegerla de las malas noticias.»

answer.text: I infer that Gran wants to protect her from bad news

feedback.es: I infer that + oración presenta tu conclusión; protect … from expresa de qué se quiere proteger.

prompt.es: Escucha la carta y elige la inferencia más prudente sobre la abuela.

choices.text: She has fully recovered and just prefers her own company.
She may be more upset by the fall than she admits.
She is annoyed with the doctor for keeping her indoors.

feedback.es: Dice que todo va bien, pero no sale desde hace una semana y las escaleras le parecen más largas: lo prudente es que la caída le ha afectado más de lo que reconoce.

origin.audio: Dear Leo, everything is fine here, so please don't worry about me. I haven't been out for a week, but the books are lovely and the neighbours have promised to look in. The doctor says it was only a small fall, although I must admit that the stairs seem longer than they used to be. Give my love to your mother, and tell her there is no need to come before the holidays. Gran

prompt.es: Relaciona cada cita con la inferencia que apoya.

pairs: Your brother called twice.
I told him you were busy.
Don't worry about me.
The neighbours will look in.

feedback.es: Cada cita es una pista distinta: las llamadas muestran interés, la excusa protege y la frase final puede esconder preocupación.

pairs: Your brother called twice.
I told him you were busy.
Don't worry about me.
The neighbours will look in.

prompt.es: Elige el rasgo de Mia que muestran esas acciones.

choices.text: She is forgetful because she repeats the same jobs daily.
She is proud because she wants everyone to notice her work.
She is reliable because she does what she promised.

answer.text: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two possible explanations. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. Both ideas are possible at first, but only one of them fits the evidence. The door was locked all night, so a stranger can't have come in. We have two possible explanations for the missing trophy. A stranger may have taken it, or the cleaner might have moved it. A stranger cannot have taken it, because the door was locked all night and the cabinet is not broken, so whoever opened it probably had a key. The cleaner has a key, worked yesterday and has no alibi for Friday evening. Since nothing else accounts for all the evidence, the most likely explanation is that the cleaner moved the trophy, perhaps to polish it. I am not certain, however, and it would be wrong to accuse her without proof. To be sure, we should ask the cleaner tomorrow and check who else holds a key.
